title: Decide if a Shared Spaces permit works for your space

paragraphs: Step-by-step
Learn about the options and responsibilities of Shared Spaces permits.
Follow these instructions to decide if a Shared Spaces permit is a good decision for your organization or business.

sections.heading: Check our permit types and options for new Shared Spaces
paragraphs: If you are applying for a new Shared Spaces permit, check our permit types and options.
We offer Shared Spaces permits for 4 different kinds of spaces:
Curb lane
Sidewalk seating (registration required, no permit)
Merchandise display (registration required, no permit)
Street closures
Learn about the types of Shared Spaces

sections.heading: Check our rules about where you can have a Shared Space
paragraphs: You cannot have Shared Spaces on all parking lanes.
Follow our updated design guidelines and rules to apply.

sections.heading: Read your Shared Spaces responsibilities
paragraphs: You must agree to our legal responsibilities to get a Shared Spaces permit.
Read your Shared Spaces responsibilities

sections.heading: Design your Shared Space
paragraphs: For the permanent program, we will require site plans of your proposed Shared Space. Follow our instructions to design a site plan that meets our rules.
Your plans must meet:
Public Works code
Transportation code
Fire code
Design your parklet or parking lane Shared Space
Design your roadway Shared Space

sections.heading: Make your space accessible
paragraphs: Follow our instructions in the Shared Spaces manual to make sure your space is accessible.

sections.heading: Check what related permits you need
paragraphs: You need other permits for outdoor entertainment, propane heaters, alcohol sales, and other activities.

sections.heading: Get your Shared Spaces permit
paragraphs: Once you decide you want to apply for a Shared Spaces permit, follow these steps to prepare your application, apply, and get your issued permit.
Get a Shared Spaces permit
